t: You're on Doughty Street, a broad, tree-lined street in Bloomsbury. It runs up from John Street, crosses Guilford Street, and ends at Mecklenburgh Square. It's named after Henry Doughty, who owned the land when the street was built. The journalist and novelist Shirley Brooks was born here. He started out in a solicitor's office, then turned to writing, joined the staff of Punch in 1851, and became its editor in 1870. The artists' model known as Dolores was also born here.
